title: FLA import: decode CPicText color effects (Tint/Alpha/Brightness) — currently always null
description:
DEFERRED (fixture-blocked). readCPicText declares colorEffect and never assigns it (flash8-binary.ts:2631, 2717-2744; TODO(1050)), unlike CPicSymbol which decodes its color-transform block. Any text field with a color effect imports with the effect dropped -> visibly wrong color. The blocking comment notes the byte position is unconfirmed; guessing risks misaligning the stream and decoding wrong text content, so this needs a real fixture FLA with a tinted text field first.

UNBLOCK PATH (assessed 2026-06-14): the blocker IS removable. flacomdoc (/tmp/flacomdoc, the byte-verified XFL->binary-FLA writer) ships color-effect writers — coloreffects/{Tint,Brightness,Alpha,Advanced}ColorEffect.java — and writes text via TimelineConverter. So a fixture can be GENERATED rather than hunted: author an XFL with a static/dynamic text field carrying a Tint (and/or Brightness/Alpha) color effect, run flacomdoc to emit a binary FLA, confirm our importer currently drops the effect, then decode the CPicText colorEffect block against flacomdoc's emitted bytes (mirror the CPicSymbol color-transform decode). Effort: build+run flacomdoc (Java), author the XFL, then the decode. Caveat to verify first: confirm flacomdoc actually emits the color-effect block for a TEXT element (color effects are normally instance-level; CPicText carrying one needs confirming in TimelineConverter) before relying on it.

Acceptance: a fixture FLA with a tinted text field imports a non-null colorEffect matching the authored tint; existing no-effect text still decodes correctly (no regression). Files: packages/core/src/fla/flash8-binary.ts:2631, 2717-2744. Do NOT guess byte offsets without the fixture (CArchive desync risk, cf task 1183). Source: discovery audit Task D; unblock path added during golden-parity session.
